true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Close the template conditional with a plain end

The tag uses `end if` without a condition instead of closing the opening conditional with `end`. This produces invalid Ruby when the ERB template is compiled, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail instead of displaying the discussion. The controller specs do not render this template and therefore miss the failure.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle RSS entries that do not have an Atom content field

Standard RSS entries commonly provide their body in `description` or `content:encoded`, rather than `content`. SimpleRSS exposes these as separate fields, so `i.content` is nil for such entries and calling scrub raises an exception. One such entry aborts the entire poll; it also prevents TopicRetriever from reaching its HTTP fallback when feed polling is enabled. Select the available content field and handle entries with no body safely.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Defer post-processing jobs until the outer transaction commits

PostCreator#create enqueues feature_topic_users and process_post before returning. Its internal transaction joins this new outer transaction, so the topic and post are still uncommitted when those jobs are submitted. A Sidekiq worker can execute them before their records are visible, and a later failure creating TopicEmbed can leave queued work for rolled-back records. Preserve atomic creation of the embed and post, but defer job submission until the outer transaction commits.

Preserve the original discussion timestamp during Disqus import

The previous PostCreator call supplied the thread's created_at timestamp, but import_remote does not accept or forward it. Imported topics and their first posts now receive the current time, while replies still retain their historical timestamps. This makes old discussions appear newly created and gives their opening posts timestamps later than their replies. Carry the source thread timestamp through the TopicEmbed import API.

Resolve relative references using URI joining

The slash-prefix substitution corrupts protocol-relative URLs: `//cdn.example/image.png` becomes a path on the article's host instead of a URL on cdn.example. It also leaves path-relative references such as `images/image.png` and `../other-page` untouched, so browsers resolve them against the forum URL. Imported articles consequently contain broken images and links. Resolve href and src values against the article URL with URI joining rather than manually prefixing slashes.

Sanitize HTML even when skipping Markdown rendering

Returning raw here bypasses HTML sanitization entirely. PollFeed passes feed HTML into TopicEmbed.import, where Nokogiri parses it but does not remove scripts or event-handler attributes. These posts use raw_html, and their cooked content is rendered unescaped. A feed item containing an onerror handler therefore introduces stored XSS under the forum's origin. Subsequent edits to imported posts bypass the same protection. This mode should skip Markdown conversion while still sanitizing HTML on every cook.

Validate redirect destinations before fetching remote articles

TopicRetriever validates only the initial URL's hostname, while open-uri follows HTTP redirects without applying that validation again. If the configured site exposes an external redirect endpoint, a caller can supply an allowed-host URL that redirects to a private-network service. Its response can then be imported into a public topic. The Referer check does not prevent requests from clients that supply that header themselves. Validate each redirect destination, including its resolved address, before issuing the request.

true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Preserve panel right alignment in the legacy flexbox fallback

The new `flexbox()` mixin falls back to `display: -webkit-box`/`-moz-box`, but those legacy box layouts treat auto margins as zero. In browsers selecting that fallback, removing `float: right` and relying on `margin-left: auto` leaves the header panel immediately after the logo/topic title instead of at the right edge. The dropdowns are positioned relative to that panel with `right: 0`, so the wide search dropdown can consequently extend off the left side of the viewport. Provide equivalent legacy-box spacing, or preserve the float layout for those browsers rather than enabling this fallback.

false_negatives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not replace an existing refresh token with a placeholder

This fallback runs for native provider responses as well as shared credentials. Office 365 explicitly permits a refresh response without a new `refresh_token`; its caller previously retained the existing token when merging the response. The helper now inserts the literal `refresh_token`, which overwrites that valid token in the database and causes the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not rotate it.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use real schema fields instead of stringifying Zod schemas

Both computed property names evaluate to the literal string `[object Object]`; they do not define arbitrary numeric or optional properties. Since Zod objects strip unknown fields by default, a normal sync response loses its expiry, refresh token, and other metadata. For example, Zoom then calculates its new expiry from an undefined `expires_in`, producing NaN. Define and preserve the actual response fields, including the expiry information consumed by each adapter.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the safeParse result

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `{ success: true, data: ... }` wrapper, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials themselves. Saving that wrapper as `credential.key` removes the token fields from the root of the stored credentials. This happens even with sharing disabled, so the next service initialization cannot load the Google credentials correctly. Persist the result's `data` instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Adapt fetch responses for callers that expect SDK or Axios results

The sync branch returns a raw fetch `Response`, but Google, Zoho CRM, and Bigin read `.data` from the result, while HubSpot treats the result itself as a parsed token object. A fetch Response has none of those token properties, regardless of the JSON returned by the endpoint. Consequently, successful sync requests throw on undefined fields or fail to install the returned tokens. Decode and adapt the response at these callers, with an explicit return contract rather than `any`.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Pass the credential owner's user ID to Bigin credential sync

The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a user ID, but this call supplies the credential row's ID. The helper sends that value as `calcomUserId`, so whenever these independent IDs differ it requests a nonexistent or different user's integration. It also incorrectly routes team credentials through user sync because their credential IDs are non-null. Pass `credential.userId` separately from the ID used for database updates.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

false_positives.candidate:
Accept the minimal sync response in the Webex adapter

The new sync helper documents a response containing only the access token and expiry, but Webex still validates that response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token lifetime. A successful response following the sync contract is therefore rejected as invalid when the access token expires. Add sync-specific decoding and retain the existing provider metadata rather than requiring native refresh-response fields.

Authenticate outbound credential-refresh requests

The token-retrieval request sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no shared-secret header, signature, or other authentication. An externally reachable parent endpoint cannot distinguish this request from an arbitrary caller supplying the same identifiers: it must either reject these calls or risk exposing users' third-party access tokens. Add an explicit server-to-server authentication mechanism to the refresh protocol.

Clear the invalid flag when replacing repaired credentials

Google, Zoom, and Webex can mark a credential `invalid: true` after an unrecoverable authentication failure. If the user reconnects in the parent application and sends fresh keys through this webhook, the update changes only `key`, leaving the same row marked invalid. The webhook reports success without restoring the connection. Clear the invalid flag when accepting valid replacement credentials.

Decode shared Lark tokens without requiring a native response envelope

The sync response is passed directly to `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>` and then read through `data.data`, including refresh-token lifetime fields. The helper's documented access-token-and-expiry response has neither Lark's `code`/`data` envelope nor that refresh-token metadata, so a valid shared-token response cannot refresh this integration. Handle the sync response separately from Lark's native refresh response.

Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce refresh path

The new code calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this module neither imports nor declares `prisma`. This fails TypeScript checking and, if checking is bypassed, throws a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce operations even when credential sharing is disabled.

Make initial credential synchronization idempotent under concurrency

The lookup and creation are separate operations with no serialization or stable upsert key. Two simultaneous deliveries for a user/app with no existing credential can both observe no row and both create one. Subsequent webhook updates modify only the first matching row, leaving the duplicate with stale tokens. Serialize creation for the logical credential or introduce an idempotent identity that can be atomically upserted.

Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint

Unlike the other modified integrations, Salesforce always posts directly to the provider and never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`. Enabling credential sharing therefore has no effect on where Salesforce obtains tokens. Credentials whose refresh tokens are managed only by the parent store fail this request instead of using the configured sync endpoint, defeating the new feature for Salesforce.

Send Zoom's app slug rather than its directory name

This sends `appSlug=zoomvideo` to the parent store, but Zoom is installed with `appId: "zoom"` and the credential webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent store keyed by that same slug cannot match the refresh request to the synced Zoom credential. Use `zoom`, consistently with installation and webhook requests.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use an environment-file replacement compatible with GNU sed

The sed -i '' syntax is BSD-specific. On Linux with GNU sed, the empty argument is treated as the sed program and the replacement expression as a filename, so an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is not updated. The script nevertheless prints its success message, leaving webhook registration pointed at the previous tunnel. Use a portable replacement or select the appropriate in-place syntax for the installed sed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

false_positives.candidate:
Refresh cache status after successful deletion

The delete-cache success handler only invokes an optional callback; it never invalidates or updates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The wrapper passes its optional onChanged callback directly through and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. Without a callback that explicitly refetches, deleting the cache therefore leaves the old timestamp and delete action visible after the success toast. Invalidate the connected-calendars query on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

Resolve backing cache records for delegated connections

When a connected calendar uses an in-memory delegation credential, its negative credential ID cannot match CalendarCache rows stored against database credentials. The existing getCachedAvailability implementation explicitly handles this case using userId and the cache key, but this status lookup only uses the displayed credential ID. Consequently, a delegated connection can serve cached availability while reporting cacheUpdatedAt as null. Because the duplicate non-delegated connection is filtered out and delegated connections cannot disconnect, the dropdown then disappears entirely, preventing these users from viewing or clearing their cache. Resolve the backing cache records for delegated connections and use that same authorized scope for deletion.

Resolve the environment file relative to the script

ENV_FILE is relative to the caller's working directory, not the script's location. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL to ../.env outside the repository, potentially creating that file, while leaving the application's configuration unchanged. Derive the repository environment-file path from BASH_SOURCE so the normal root-level invocation updates the intended file.

Keep the registered metric-alert handler instantiable

MetricAlertFire still registers this class, and Detector.detector_handler instantiates registered handlers, so accessing the handler for a detector with type='metric_alert_fire' now raises TypeError. process_detectors does not catch this exception, so that detector aborts the batch instead of retaining the previous no-op behavior. Implement the required methods or retain a concrete placeholder returning an empty dict.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.

Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.

false_positives.candidate:
Build the expected occurrence with the evaluated group key

TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence with group_key='val1', but invokes evaluate_group_key_value with group_key='group_key'. The helper incorporates that key into the occurrence fingerprint, so the expected fingerprint ends in ':val1' while the actual fingerprint ends in ':group_key'. The result equality assertion therefore fails even with the correct implementation. Build the expected occurrence using 'group_key'.

true_positives.golden_comment: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Wait for flushing with an unpatched synchronization mechanism

test_basic replaces time.sleep with a no-op at line 15, so this added sleep does not wait for the flusher to observe the advanced drift. The following join() sets the worker's stopped flag immediately. Depending on thread scheduling, the worker can exit without emitting the expected segment, leaving the messages assertion flaky. Wait for the produced message or a completion event before joining, using an unpatched synchronization primitive.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Recognize spawn-context processes before killing unhealthy workers

Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the default-context multiprocessing.Process class. This condition is therefore false for production workers. When a worker hangs, the manager starts a replacement without killing the original and overwrites its tracked reference. The original can remain stuck or resume flushing alongside its replacement. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the actual context's Process class; the termination guard in join() has the same problem.

true_positives.golden_comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Clean up every worker even after the join deadline expires

If next_step.join() consumes the timeout, or waiting for one worker exhausts it, this break skips cleanup of all remaining workers. Setting stopped only requests an exit between flush iterations, so workers blocked in Redis operations or Kafka futures can survive the rebalance and overlap the replacement strategy. The deadline should limit graceful waiting, but every remaining process still needs forced termination and cleanup.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Make device admission atomic across requests

CountDevices and the subsequent upsert run in separate database sessions without synchronization. With one slot remaining, concurrent requests from different new devices can all observe a count below the limit and then all insert successfully. Those excess devices subsequently qualify for updates and can remain admitted indefinitely. Serialize the count-and-admit operation at the database level so the limit also holds across Grafana instances.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache devices only after admission succeeds

tagDeviceUI caches the device before CreateOrUpdateDevice checks the limit. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, that cache entry remains for 29 minutes. A second request with the rejected device ID therefore returns nil from the cache check, and Anonymous.Authenticate grants access without enforcing the limit. Simply retrying bypasses the restriction. Populate the cache only after a successful store operation, and test repeated requests from a rejected device.

The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

false_positives.candidate:
Do not treat a missing device ID as successful admission

Anonymous authentication now relies on TagDevice to reject requests beyond the limit, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. Consequently, even with the configured limit exhausted, a caller can omit this client-controlled header and receive an anonymous identity for API requests without being counted or checked. Limited anonymous access needs an admission path for requests without a device ID rather than treating them as admitted.

Make the device limit configurable through environment overrides

The new device_limit key is read from the raw INI section but is not added to conf/defaults.ini. Grafana's normal environment-override pass visits keys already present in the loaded configuration, so setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone leaves this value at 0 and silently disables enforcement. Add the key to the defaults or read it through SectionWithEnvOverrides, with a test covering an environment-only configuration.

The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

Read-only group permission authorizes group creation

canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-Groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses this check to authorize POST /groups, so an administrator granted only read access can create groups or move existing subgroups to the top level. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

Authorization resource IDs are used as group IDs

groupResource.getId() is the authorization resource's generated ID, not the GroupModel ID stored in its name. Passing it to hasPermission() therefore looks up the wrong name, and adding it to granted supplies invalid IDs to user membership queries. In particular, a view-members or manage-members grant on all Groups returns the aggregate authorization resource's UUID; UsersResource then filters by that UUID and returns no users, and /users/count is also incorrect. Collect actual group IDs and handle the aggregate Groups resource separately.

The group-member creation fallback still checks only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, the V1 feature flag. With V2 enabled, an administrator granted the new manage-members and manage-membership scopes on a group receives 403 from POST /users even when the representation assigns the new user only to that authorized group: canCreateGroupMembers() exits before evaluating those permissions. Allow this fallback for V2 as well and cover group-scoped user creation in the new tests.

Remove exhausted credentials from their actual storage

The new lookup can return a credential owned by an external user-storage provider, but the exhaustion branch below still passes its ID to removeStoredCredentialById, which only deletes Keycloak-stored credentials. For a provider that keeps its credential record configured after consuming the final code, the exhausted record therefore remains. Remove the existing local recovery-code credential after successfully replacing it in user storage, and cover this migration/regeneration case in a test.
